Opinions:

Since it has happened, lots of jobs have been lots and industry has moved elsewhere in order to avoid tax rates importing into Europe and other issues. Additionally, we have more governance over our own laws which is not a good thing as the UK government can now make decisions without being held accountable to the EU standards.

Overall is has started a downfall to the UK's economy.

The inflation is getting out of hands currently and it doesn't seem like there will be and end to it any time soon in fact it seems that it will just worsen year by year. I think the UK thought they can be much more independent then what they're actually capable of.

A small group of people each wrote an opinion on the question below.

Question: Does austerity work?

Opinions:
1. i think it has the potential to work, but for some countries it is not feasible within the modern day. relying on other countries does bring problems regarding trust, money,  disagreements can arise. to achieve austerity we need a good economy and politicians making good decisions which feels impossible at the moment. people in positions of power will be unable to achieve austerity due to insecurities and bad decisions, as well as budgeting issues
2. Difficult one this. I want to say no - our current Government in the UK is a proven fact that austerity doesn't work, they've managed to run this ecomony into the ground, blamed it on a host of other factors, such as "wokeness" and really not understanding that the people just want to eat, be warm and healthy but instead they continue to treat us like garbage. A small group of people each wrote an opinion on the question below.

Question: Should children over the age of 14 have a legally binding voice in custody cases when parents divorce?

Opinions:
1. Yes, although having not been through anything like that myself I don't really know to what extent. Presumably there will be some safeguarding issues if the child ends up with a parent that they do not want to be with, and it seems that they would be old enough at that point to be able to make a reasoned decision.
2. I am conflicted with this question, I am not sure if the age is appropriate or if it should be higher. However I do believe that the child should have some say in the matter as it is very important that their opinion is made clear.
3. Yes, I believe that children 14+ are old enough to have a say in who they want to live with. Children are often used as pawns in divorce and their best interests are often forgotten about. I believe they should be able to express their opinions and have them taken seriously in a court of law.
4. I don't know whether they should if I am honest. I think they should get a voice, but I don't know whether it should be legally binding. 14 is a young age and they could be influenced by other people. They would also be quite affected by the divorce, so might not have a Clear head or be thinking straight.
5. I feel like their opinions should be heard and considered, however the way they see things or feel towards things shouldnt be the most important factor or hold alot of weight as a 14 year old can be naive and have external factors that influence what they say about the situation. A marriage is between the two individuals I understand the child is also being affected but the vows were between the couple and it is their duty to weigh up the circumstances not a childs.
